prompt:
Portrait-format stained-glass window seen from inside a Gothic church, looking toward a tall two-light window. Medieval West Flemish church interior, dim stone tracery, lead cames, slightly cartoonish Gothic illustration, not photorealistic.

Composition: two tall lancets side by side beneath one circular rose window. Stone mullion between the lancets. Pointed arches. Thick black lead lines dividing the glass into irregular medieval panes. Jewel colors: deep blue, ruby red, gold, emerald, amber, white, and violet. Light coming through the glass from outside, glowing against a dark church interior. No modern objects, no text except the inscriptions specified below.

Left lancet — French charge: French knights in mail and surcoats, fleur-de-lis on shields and horse trappings, charging on horseback from the upper left toward the lower right. The foremost horse is stumbling and falling into a water-filled ditch or brook that cuts across the bottom of the panel. Riders behind press forward, lances angled down. Cartoonish but period-correct faces, helmets, and horse tack. Banner of France: blue field with gold fleurs-de-lis, carried among the knights.

Right lancet — Flemish militia: Flemish townsmen on foot, no horses, standing firm on the near side of the ditch. They hold goedendags (wooden clubs with a spike) and long pikes angled toward the falling French horse. Simple tunics, kettle hats or mail coifs, determined cartoon faces. Banner of Flanders: yellow field with a black lion, held upright among the militia. Golden spurs scattered in the grass and mud at their feet, clearly readable as spurs, not generic jewelry.

Rose window: circular tracery filled with the lion of Flanders, black lion rampant on gold, simplified so it reads at a distance. Small colored roundels around the lion.

Inscriptions in Gothic blackletter on the glass, one line each, clearly legible:
Left lancet base: GULDENSPORENSLAG
Right lancet base: KORTRIJK 1302

Style notes: hand-painted stained glass, uneven glass texture, soldered lead, slight distortion of figures through old glass, flat medieval perspective, bold outlines, limited shading. Battle of the Golden Spurs, Kortrijk (Courtrai), 11 July 1302, told as one church window. No gore beyond the falling horse and clash of weapons. No signatures, no watermarks, no extra captions.
